description: Arbalette is a serpentine form characteristic of the finest Louis XV commodes and consoles. Our Arbalette chair exhibits a concave center portion with convex edges to form a reverse serpentine shape. The sleek back and arms are often adorned and finished with a nailhead trim. The back legs have a unique shape while the front legs taper to a cylindrical shape.

description: King George III was still a bachelor when he ascended the throne of Great Britain. He married the seventeen year old Princess Charlotte, the youngest daughter of Duke Charles of Mecklenburg-Strelitz in 1761. In 1762, the new queen gave birth to her first child, the Prince of Wales who would later be known as George IV. Our Charlotte chair is named after the queen who was responsible for the interior decoration of their residence at Windsor. This frame features and boasts a boxed welt design which borders its sides, top, and seat.

description: The 17th and 18th centuries include what is known as the Age of Libraries. The first important library with complete access to the public was Chetham's library in Manchester, England. It boasts, as standard, a finely executed hand button tufted inside back and a single welt throughout the frame.

description: The saying goes there is nothing new under the sun but the function of design is to draw from, reinterpret, and recast the old into the new. Our contemporary Dolce chair draws inspiration from the simple forms of the late 20th century. Working with a gently curved and extended back, we kept things simple yet elegant by ending with a modified Duncan Fiffe leg at the rear, and a gently tapered leg at the front. The armchair is found on the opposite folio.
